extra.message: GET /api/dashboard passes the caller-controlled clinic_layout cookie here. Its parsed properties become unrestricted User updates. Any authenticated patient can supply {"role":"clinic_admin"} to gain administrative privileges; subsequent authorization reads this role from the database.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The format query parameter from /api/documents/[id]/convert is interpolated into an execSync shell command without validation or escaping, allowing authorized staff to execute arbitrary commands. Stored sourcePath values also retain user-controlled upload extensions, whose shell substitutions remain executable inside double quotes.

POST /api/prescriptions/[id]/label passes the request's layoutPreset directly into this command. Executing it through sh with shell:true allows staff who can access a prescription to inject shell operators and execute arbitrary server commands.

The formName query parameter from /api/documents/forms is joined to FORMS_DIR without a containment check. Any authenticated user can supply ../ components to read accessible files outside the forms directory. The target filename must end in the appended .pdf extension.

The appointments export passes the caller-controlled clinic_batch cookie as batchId. Traversal components escape CACHE_DIR, allowing an authenticated clinic administrator to create or overwrite writable .csv files elsewhere on the server with export contents.

When SESSION_SECRET is unset, including in production, iron-session uses a publicly known hardcoded key. An attacker can forge clinic_portal_session cookies containing another active user's ID and impersonate that user, including an administrator.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: An unset PARTNER_SIGNING_KEY silently selects an empty HMAC key. Attackers can generate signatures accepted by admitReferralClaim and submit forged claims to /api/referrals/resolve, changing a patient's insuranceProvider without authorization for that patient.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: readReferralClaim only decodes the payload and never verifies its signature or expiration. /api/referrals/intake trusts patientExternalId and partnerId from this payload to select and update a patient and return their identity. Any authenticated caller can fabricate claims for other patients.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: The q parameter from /api/providers/coverage-directory is interpolated directly into an LDAP filter. Staff can inject LDAP metacharacters to change filter semantics. URL encoding in DirectoryClient.search protects the HTTP URL, but does not escape LDAP syntax.

POST /api/appointments/series takes occurrences from X-Series-Occurrences without an upper bound. Each iteration inserts an appointment and retains its ID in memory. A patient can request an enormous series, exhausting database storage, memory, and processing capacity.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The action checks patient access but never authorizes the requested status or validates the transition. Patients can invoke it directly to mark their own appointments completed or checked_in, or reactivate cancelled appointments, although the UI permits patients only to cancel scheduled/requested appointments.

uploadDocumentAction accepts a supplied patientId without checking ownership or clinician assignment, then uses it in prisma.document.create. Any authenticated patient can attach documents to another patient's chart. The separate /api/documents POST handler performs this check, but the server action bypasses it.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: sendMessageAction trusts patientId from FormData and creates a message against that patient without an ownership or assignment check. Patients and unassigned clinicians can insert messages into another patient's record.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /api/messages prioritizes the request's patientId over the authenticated patient's profile and performs no record authorization. An authenticated caller can create messages attached to another patient's chart.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: createPrescriptionAction authorizes patientId but independently accepts visitSummaryId without checking that the summary belongs to that patient or is accessible to the clinician. A clinician can attach a prescription to another patient's visit summary, corrupting the clinical record returned with that appointment.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Clinician assignment checks run only when user.provider exists; otherwise full chart access is allowed. Both role-change implementations can promote a patient or front-desk account to clinician without creating a Provider. Such accounts bypass assignment restrictions. The patient chart page and patient, document, and prescription list endpoints contain the same fail-open condition.

A patient account without a PatientProfile produces patientId:undefined, which leaves the Prisma query unscoped. Admin role changes can create this state by changing a staff account to patient without creating a profile. The account can then read other patients' prescriptions; analogous omissions affect appointment, message, dashboard, and search queries.

The letterhead endpoint writes arbitrary uploaded bytes under the original filename into public/branding, without validating file type or extension. An administrator can upload HTML or SVG containing scripts that execute under the portal's origin when another user opens the served asset.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: When RECORD_RELEASE_KEY is absent, both CBC and GCM envelope handlers use a publicly known constant key. Attackers can decrypt envelopes and forge release claims accepted by the external-release and partner-release endpoints. There is no production guard or startup failure.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Caller-supplied ciphertext is decrypted with unauthenticated AES-CBC. Padding failures produce a different error from valid-padding/invalid-JSON failures, and /api/documents/external-release returns these messages verbatim. Repeated chosen-ciphertext requests provide a padding oracle for recovering encrypted envelope contents.

The server action accepts visibility:internal_only from any authenticated caller and persists it without a role check. Patients can insert messages into the staff-only channel despite the UI restriction and the API handler's explicit patient_visible enforcement.

PATCH checks authorization only when recipientId is non-null. Any authenticated user knowing the ID of a message with no recipient can mark it read, including another patient's or an internal-only message. Patient ownership, visibility, and clinician assignment are never checked.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Patients authorized for an appointment receive its visit summary regardless of draft/released status, including diagnosis and clinician notes. This bypasses the release restriction enforced by the patient chart endpoint and exposes notes before the clinician releases them.

The server-rendered prescription page scopes records only for patients. Clinicians receive prescriptions for unassigned patients, including medication, dosage, instructions, and refill notes. This bypasses the assignment filter implemented in /api/prescriptions.

The appointment list restricts patients but applies no assignment restriction to clinicians. A clinician can list or filter another patient's appointments and obtain reasons, notes, contact details, and cancellation information even when the individual appointment endpoint denies access.

All staff, including clinicians, receive an empty appointment scope. The dashboard exposes recent appointments for unassigned patients, including names and visit reasons. src/app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx independently uses the same unrestricted staff query.

Search permits every staff member to query patients without clinician-assignment restrictions. Its appointment, message, and document queries likewise restrict only patient accounts. Clinicians can search unassigned patients' identities, visit reasons, message contents, and document metadata. searchAction in src/app/actions/actions.ts has the same omission.

GET /api/messages restricts patient accounts but applies no patient-assignment or recipient restriction to clinicians. Clinicians can retrieve full messages and internal notes concerning unassigned patients, bypassing authorization enforced by the individual message endpoint.

The audit API rejects only patients, allowing front-desk staff and clinicians to retrieve the entire clinic audit trail, including prescription details, patient identifiers, user emails, IP addresses, and user agents. It has neither the admin restriction of /admin/audit nor a clinician-assignment scope.

The patient chart API returns auditLogs to patient accounts, including internal details and staff identity/email information. The chart UI explicitly restricts audit history to staff, but the API applies no corresponding role restriction.

CSV serialization escapes delimiters but leaves spreadsheet formula prefixes intact. Patients control exported names and appointment reasons and can submit values beginning with =, +, -, or @ that spreadsheet applications interpret as formulas when an administrator opens the export. The visits export repeats this serialization at lines 107-110.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: CLEARINGHOUSE_BASE defaults to an http:// partner address. Releasing a visit summary sends the patient's ID, diagnosis, provider ID, and clearinghouse credential over this unencrypted connection when CLEARINGHOUSE_URL is unset, exposing them to network interception and modification.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The clearinghouse API key is placed in the request URL query string alongside the patient ID. URLs are exposed to request logging and monitoring at the partner and intermediary infrastructure; configuring HTTPS does not remove the credential from those URLs.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of HTTP Request With Sensitive Query String

extra.message: The care assistant defaults to an unencrypted HTTP gateway and transmits complete patient follow-up drafts and feedback supplied through /api/messages/assistant. Confidential patient content in these drafts can be intercepted or altered by an observer on the gateway network.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The q parameter from /api/providers/coverage-directory is inserted verbatim into a console log entry. Staff can include newline and control characters to forge additional log entries or obscure the actual search activity.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: Setting X-Clinic-Channel: ops-console causes the appointments export to return raw exception messages, stack traces, and context. Any caller authorized to export can enable this disclosure and trigger it with an invalid date, exposing server paths and database-driver diagnostics without separate operations privileges.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The companion access credential is generated from Math.random and truncated to eight base-36 characters. This noncryptographic generator is unsuitable for a bearer secret subsequently used to authorize access to appointment status and visit reasons.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: Companion sessions are accepted solely by matching a stored code. There is no expiration timestamp or appointment-state check, and logout does not delete the code. A retained or stolen companion cookie can continue retrieving appointment information indefinitely until someone explicitly issues a replacement.

Logout destroys only the browser's iron-session cookie. getCurrentUser accepts any otherwise-valid sealed cookie for an active user and checks no revocation record or session version. A copied session cookie remains usable after the legitimate user logs out, until its original expiration.

loginAction performs password verification without tracking failures, throttling attempts, or locking accounts. No application-level limiter exists in the middleware or authentication helpers. Attackers can make unlimited password guesses; switchWorkstationUserAction has the same omission.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: The application's runtime database client always authenticates as postgres using the hardcoded password postgres. DATABASE_URL is ignored here, so configuring a secure connection elsewhere does not replace this known credential. Anyone able to reach this database can attempt authentication with the published account.

The companion_view cookie contains the appointment access credential but is set without HttpOnly or Secure. Same-origin JavaScript can read it, and the browser can transmit it over HTTP, exposing a reusable credential.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag
CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without Secure Attribute

extra.message: The seed creates administrator, clinician, front-desk, and patient accounts with the shared password password123. The login page publicly displays these credentials. Any deployment retaining the seeded accounts permits login with known passwords; the seed has no environment restriction.

Successful clinical-document downloads return file contents without creating an audit entry. Patient chart reads and message reads likewise omit access logging. Staff or compromised accounts can access sensitive records without the per-record access trail required by the application's audit workflow.

unassignPatientFromProviderAction deletes patient-provider authorization assignments without recording the actor or affected relationship in the audit log. Unlike the reassignment action, this security-relevant permission change leaves no audit trail.
